name: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene

pubchem.title: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene
pubchem.description: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene is a bicyclic sesquiterpene that is 1-methylidenedecahydronaphthalene carrying additional methyl and isopropylidene substituents at positions 4a and 7 respectively. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a sesquiterpene, a polycyclic olefin and a carbobicyclic compound. It derives from a hydride of a eudesmane.

evidence: Measured in 6 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.31–9.08% of total volatiles (0.062–1.82mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene is a bicyclic sesquiterpene, a class of complex aromatic molecules often responsible for the rich scents and flavors of botanical extracts. As a natural plant metabolite, it is a hydrocarbon that contributes to the chemical profile of the leaves, fruits, and resins where it is found.
consumer_summary.found_in: You can find this molecule in familiar plants like hops (Humulus lupulus), which are famously used to brew beer, and the tropical fruit-bearing Surinam cherry (Eugenia uniflora).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Currently, researchers are primarily interested in Selina-4(15),7(11)-diene as a structural component of plant essential oils and resins. Because it is a naturally occurring sesquiterpene found in agriculturally important plants like hops, it helps chemists understand the complex chemical makeup and metabolic pathways of these species. At present, there is no specific medical or pharmacological research literature available for this compound (Oxford level 5, chemical profiling).
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: There is currently no published pharmacological or clinical evidence available for this molecule; it is known primarily through the chemical profiling of plants.
